prompt.en: A Yagi element is not connected to the feedline but is coupled by nearby RF fields. What is it called?

explanation.en: A parasitic element is energized by coupling from the driven element rather than direct feedline connection.

prompt.en: A roof-mounted quarter-wave vertical is centred on a vehicle roof. Which prediction fits the horizontal pattern?

text.en: No compass direction is favoured because the vertical element is symmetric around its axis
The strongest direction is off the hood because the vehicle points that way
The strongest direction is straight overhead, so nearby ground stations are in a null
The feedline direction steers the main lobe unless the coax is exactly 50 ohms

explanation.en: The vertical element is symmetric around its upright axis, so the simple horizontal pattern does not favour one compass direction over another.

prompt.en: A club stacks an identical pair of beams and feeds them from the same transmitter. What does the ideal gain increase mean?

text.en: The main-direction power density is roughly doubled because the pattern is concentrated
The antenna pair radiates twice the transmitter power into all directions
The stacked array turns a poor impedance match into a perfect one
The rear lobe becomes the main source of forward gain

explanation.en: Stacking an identical pair can roughly double power density in the main direction before losses by narrowing and shaping the pattern; it does not create extra transmitter power.
